key_insight: Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation can preserve symmetry exactly when written with Hermitian excitation operators for Abelian symmetries, but non-Abelian symmetries need extra operator processing to reduce symmetry breaking.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum chemistry and quantum phase estimation workflows a practical way to improve symmetry fidelity, which can lower simulation error and make classical pretesting of quantum algorithms more reliable.
method: Rewrite the Hamiltonian using Hermitian excitation operators.
Map each operator to sums of commuting Pauli strings to preserve Abelian symmetries under Trotterization.
Use operator kirigami: orthogonal projection to cut non-commuting sums and unitary rotations to fold terms together for non-Abelian cases.
evidence_signal: The authors tested operator pools on small molecules and basis sets, comparing symmetry-conserving choices and Trotter order, and found that second-order Trotterization removed the larger symmetry-related errors.
watch_item: Symmetries tied to non-Abelian groups are not fully conserved by simple Trotterized Hermitian excitation operators, so careful operator design or higher-order Trotterization is still needed.
paper_title: Symmetry conservation with Trotterization and Quantum Phase Estimation
